section.content: The present invention relates to a lithium ion battery. Specifically, the lithium ion battery comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, electrolyte and a diaphragm, and is characterized in that: the positive pole piece comprises aluminum foil as a positive current collector, and the content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil per unit area is 0.009g/m2～0.021g/m2The electrolyte contains a first lithium salt and an additive A, the first lithium salt is a fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt, and the amount of the fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt is 30 mol% or more relative to the total molar amount of lithium salts in the electrolyte; the additive A is a phosphate compound containing unsaturated bonds and contains-SO2-at least one of a cyclic compound of a bond and a silicone oxide compound containing an unsaturated branch. The lithium ion battery has the excellent performances of high capacity, high dynamic performance, long cycle life, less high-temperature gas production and the like.

Lithium ion batteryTechnical Field

The invention belongs to the technical field of electrochemistry. More particularly, the present invention relates to a lithium ion battery.

Background

The lithium ion battery has the advantages of high voltage platform, less self-discharge, high output power, no memory effect, long cycle life, less environmental pollution and the like, so that the lithium ion battery is widely applied to electric automobiles and consumer products.

With the expansion of the application range, especially with the popularization of smart phones and electric vehicles, the demand for high energy density lithium ion batteries is increasing. The cell energy density can be increased by two ways: the nickel content of the battery anode material is increased, and the battery charging voltage is increased. In recent years, the use of high nickel cathode materials to replace the conventional lithium cobalt cathode to improve the capacity density of the battery has been widely used in the industry.

However, in actual use, it was found that the power performance, service life and high-temperature storage performance of the battery were seriously impaired when the above-described two approaches were taken. When the positive electrode active material is a high-nickel positive electrode active material, the structural stability of the positive electrode is reduced due to the increase of the nickel content, and the electrode/electrolyte interface is unstable in the circulating storage process, so that the electrolyte is continuously oxidized and decomposed at the positive electrode. The charging voltage of the battery is improved, the cathode potential is raised during charging, and the electrolyte is easier to be oxidized and decomposed. Therefore, two ways of improving the energy density of the battery (including improving the nickel content of the battery anode material and improving the charging voltage of the battery) can cause the oxidative decomposition of the electrolyte to be intensified, electrolyte by-products are covered on an electrode/electrolyte interface, so that the SEI film is continuously thickened, the interface impedance is increased, and the power performance of the battery is further deteriorated.

Therefore, there is a need to develop a lithium ion battery having improved battery capacity and kinetic properties, while having a long cycle life, higher power performance and high temperature storage performance.

Summary of The Invention

One object of the present invention is: a high capacity battery having high dynamic performance, long cycle life and low high temperature gas production is provided.

In order to achieve the above object, the present invention provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive electrode plate, a negative electrode plate, an electrolyte and a diaphragm, wherein the positive electrode plate comprises an aluminum foil as a positive electrode current collector, and the content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil per unit area is 0.009g/m2～0.021g/m2The electrolyte comprises a first lithium salt and an additive A, wherein the first lithium salt is a fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt, and the molar amount of the fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt is 30 mol% or more relative to the total molar amount of lithium salts in the electrolyte; the additive A is a phosphate compound containing unsaturated bonds and contains-SO2-at least one of a cyclic compound of a bond and a silicone oxide compound containing an unsaturated branch.

The inventor finds that the electrolyte contains fluorine-containing lithium sulfonylimide as a first lithium salt and an additive A, and the content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil of the positive current collector with a limited unit area is in a specific range, so that the comprehensive performance of a battery cell can be effectively improved. Compared with the prior art, the invention at least comprises one or more of the following beneficial effects: the low-temperature discharge resistance is obviously reduced, the dynamic performance is high, the high-temperature storage gas production is reduced, the cycle life is long, and the energy density of the battery is high. In particular, the inventors have found that, by adopting the specific combination of the present invention, the gas generation during storage of the lithium ion battery at high temperature (above 80 ℃) can be significantly reduced; the cycle life becomes long; and/or improved kinetic performance at low temperatures (-below 20 ℃).

Detailed Description

The term "optionally substituted" or "optionally substituted" in the context of describing groups or compounds herein is meant to encompass both substituted and unsubstituted. Likewise, the term "optionally fluoro substituted" or "optionally fluoro substituted" is meant to include both fluoro substituted and unsubstituted fluoro substituted. For example, optionally substituted alkyl includes unsubstituted alkyl and alkyl substituted with one or more substituents.

The term "halo derivative" in the context of describing a group or compound herein refers to a group or compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms are replaced with a halogen atom (e.g., including chlorine, fluorine, bromine, and the like). Preferably, the halogenated derivative is a fluorinated derivative. More preferably, the fluorinated derivative is perfluorinated or partially fluorinated. For example, fluoro derivatives of methyl include-CF3、-CHF2and-CH2F。

The battery according to the present invention is explained in detail below.

The invention provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, electrolyte and a diaphragm, wherein the positive pole piece comprises an aluminum foil as a positive current collector, and the content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil in unit area is 0.009g/m2～0.021g/m2The electrolyte contains a first lithium salt and an additive A, the first lithium salt is a fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt, and the molar amount of the fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt is 30 mol% or more relative to the total molar amount of lithium salts in the electrolyte(ii) a The additive A is a phosphate compound containing unsaturated bonds and contains-SO2-at least one of a cyclic compound of a bond and a silicone oxide compound containing an unsaturated branch.

The amount of the lithium salt of fluorosulfonylimide is 30 mol% or more, preferably 40 mol% or more, and more preferably 50 to 70 mol% relative to the total molar amount of the lithium salt in the electrolyte. The fluorine-containing lithium sulfonimide salt used in the present invention is used as a main lithium salt, and very advantageous effects are obtained. ByDue to the structural characteristics of the fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt, the lithium salt has higher conductivity at normal temperature and is more conventional than the conventional lithium salt (LiPF)6) More stable and less sensitive to water and temperature. Therefore, the lithium salt of the fluorine-containing sulfimide has high chemical stability and electrochemical stability, and can be used for improving the stability and power performance of the electrolyte.

More preferably, the additive A in the present invention is a phosphate ester compound containing an unsaturated bond and containing-SO, the reduction potential of which in the electrolyte is in the range of 1.2V to 0.6V2-at least one of a cyclic compound of a bond and a silicone oxide compound containing an unsaturated branch.

In the field of lithium ion batteries, the positive current collector is typically an aluminum metal foil. The foil can be divided into pure aluminum foil and aluminum alloy foil according to the relative content of Al element and other elements in the foil. In pure aluminum foil, a certain content of impurity copper element is inevitably present; for the aluminum alloy foil, the diameter and the crystalline phase of a crystallization product of the aluminum foil are effectively changed by adding various heterogeneous elements (such as copper, manganese, silicon, iron and the like), so that the aluminum alloy foil has the technical advantages of higher mechanical strength and adjustable resistivity compared with a pure aluminum foil. The inventor finds out through research that: in the electrolyte environment of high-concentration fluorine-containing lithium sulfonimide, no matter the positive current collector adopts pure aluminum foil or aluminum alloy foil, the corrosion resistance of the surface of the base material is closely related to the content of copper element in the base material in unit area, and the long-term cycle life and the power performance of the lithium ion battery are influenced. When the electrolyte containing the additive A is matched with the aluminum foil with the impurity element copper atom content in a specific range in unit area, the corrosion resistance of the aluminum foil can be further improved, the corrosivity of the high-concentration fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt electrolyte to the aluminum foil is reduced, the mechanical strength of the aluminum foil is ensured, and the cycle performance of the battery is improved. The inventor thinks that the aluminum foil can avoid the problem of overhigh extensibility of the current collector in the cold pressing process of the pole piece, and obviously reduces the conditions of micro fracture and the like of the aluminum foil in the circulation process of the battery. The inventor believes that the corrosion resistance of the positive electrode current collector to the electrolyte is improved by limiting the unit area content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil; meanwhile, by adopting the electrolyte containing the specific additive A (preferably, the reduction potential of the additive A in the electrolyte is between 1.2V and 0.6V), the additive can be reduced and decomposed when the corrosion potential of the fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt (such as LFSI) is not reached, so that a film is formed on the surface of the positive electrode active material, and the decomposition product of the additive can form a compact protective layer on the surface of the aluminum foil which is not covered with the positive electrode active material (such as accidental coating stripping), so that the reaction activity of impurity ion sites is reduced, and the corrosion resistance of the aluminum foil is improved.

In some preferred embodiments, the aluminum foil has a content of impurity copper atoms per unit area of less than 0.021g/m2. Further preferably, the content of impurity copper atoms in the aluminum foil per unit area is less than 0.018g/m2、0.015g/m2. In some preferred embodiments, the aluminum foil has a copper atom impurity content of not less than 0.008g/m per unit area2More preferably not less than 0.009g/m2. In some exemplary embodiments, the content of impurity copper atoms per unit area of the aluminum foil is 0.01g/m2、0.013g/m2、0.016g/m2Or 0.020g/m2. The inventors found that the content of impurity copper atoms per unit area of the aluminum foil is within a certain range (e.g., 0.013 g/m)2To 0.021g/m2Within range), the high temperature storage gassing performance and cycle performance of the battery are not significantly affected. However, as the copper atom content is further reduced, the mechanical properties of the aluminum foil are affected, and the high-temperature storage gas generation performance and the cycle performance are deteriorated to some extent. And when the copper atom content is too high, the corrosion resistance of the aluminum foil is deteriorated. Therefore, by controlling the content of impurity copper atoms in the aluminum foil in unit area, excellent balance can be obtained between the high-temperature gas production performance and the cycle performance of the battery.

In some preferred embodiments, the thickness of the aluminum foil (including pure aluminum foil and aluminum alloy foil) is in the range of 6 μm to 16 μm, preferably 8 μm to 15 μm.

the inventors found that the compounds represented by formulae 2 to 6 in the electrolyte solution contain at least one of a phosphorus-oxygen bond, a sulfur-oxygen bond, and a silicon-oxygen bond, and also contain an unsaturated bond branched chain, so that the SEI film formed on the surface of the positive electrode active material layer has high density and good toughness, and can effectively inhibit oxidative decomposition of the electrolyte solution. Meanwhile, the reduction potential of the compounds of formulae 2 to 6 in the electrolyte is between 1.2V and 0.6V, and the compounds can be reductively decomposed before reaching the corrosion potential of the fluorine-containing lithium sulfonimide salt (such as LFSI), and the reaction product can be attached to the exposed area of the current collector not covered by the positive active material, thereby inhibiting the corrosion of the current collector by the electrolyte (especially high-concentration salt).

In some preferred embodiments, the mass percentage of the additive a is 0.01 wt% to 5 wt% with respect to the total weight of the electrolyte. More preferably, the mass percent of the additive A in the electrolyte is 0.1-3.5 wt%. More preferably, the mass percent of the additive A in the electrolyte is 0.12-2.8 wt%. The inventor finds that when the relative content of the additive A in the electrolyte is in the range, an interfacial film with a stable structure and high toughness can be formed on the surface of the positive electrode plate, so that the side reaction of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive electrode plate can be effectively inhibited, the corrosion of high-concentration salt to an aluminum foil can be effectively inhibited, the increase of the interfacial impedance of a battery cell is not obvious, and the power performance of the battery cell is not influenced.

In some preferred embodiments, the electrolyte may further include a second lithium salt. The second lithium salt may be at least one selected from inorganic lithium salts and organic lithium salts. The second lithium salt may be selected from LiPF6、LiBF4、LiSbF6、LiAsF6、LiClO4、LiN(C2F5SO2)2、LiN(CF3SO2)2、CF3SO3Li、LiC(CF3SO2)3And LiB (C)2O4)2One or more of (a). More preferably, the second lithium salt comprises LiPF6And LiBF4At least one of (1). Particularly preferably, the second lithium salt is or comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate.

In some preferred embodiments, the molar ratio of the first lithium salt to the second lithium salt is in the range of 1:1 to 20:1, more preferably in the range of 1.2:1 to 10:1, and even more preferably in the range of 6:4 to 9: 1. For example, the molar ratio of the first lithium salt to the second lithium salt may be 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 5:1, 6:1, 7:3, or 8: 1.

The inventor finds that when the inorganic lithium salt containing fluorine is used as the second lithium salt and is charged for the first time, partial lithium salt is decomposed to generate fluorine ions, and the fluorine ions react with the aluminum foil to generate an aluminum fluoride passivation layer, so that the aluminum foil corrosion can be inhibited. Researches show that when the content of the inorganic fluorine-containing lithium salt in the total lithium salt is more than 10 mol%, the corrosion of the aluminum foil can be effectively inhibited. However, when the content of the inorganic fluorine-containing lithium salt is too large as a main lithium salt, the film forming effect at the cathode is poor, and thus the gas generation at high temperature storage is deteriorated. Therefore, when the fluorine-containing lithium sulfonimide salt is used as the first lithium salt and the inorganic fluorine-containing lithium salt is used as the second lithium salt, the problems of conductivity of the electrolyte and corrosion of the aluminum foil can be solved.

Preferably, the total concentration of the lithium salt in the electrolyte may be 0.5 to 2.0mol/L, and more preferably may be 0.6 to 1.8mol/L, 0.7 to 1.7mol/L, and 0.8 to 1.5 mol/L. Specifically, the total concentration of the lithium salt in the electrolyte may be about 0.5mol/L, 0.6mol/L, 0.7mol/L, 0.8mol/L, 0.9mol/L, 1.0mol/L, 1.1mol/L, 1.2mol/L, 1.3mol/L, 1.4mol/L, 1.5mol/L, 1.6mol/L, 1.7mol/L, 1.8mol/L, 1.9mol/L, 2.0 mol/L.

In some exemplary embodiments, the electrolyte has a conductivity of 8 mS-cm-1、8.5mS·cm-1、9.0mS·cm-1Or 9.5 mS. cm-1。

In the invention, the infiltration coefficient of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece is in the range of 0.9-3.0 mug/s, preferably in the range of 1.0-2.8 mug/s. The inventor finds that the corrosion of the electrolyte to the aluminum foil can be further reduced by controlling the infiltration coefficient of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece. Because the infiltration coefficient of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece is high, the decomposition product of the additive A can quickly enter the positive active material layer and reach the positive current collector, and a compact protective layer is formed on the area, which is not covered by the positive active material particles, on the surface of the aluminum foil, so that the corrosion problem of high-concentration fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt on the aluminum foil can be inhibited to a certain extent, the DCR of the lithium ion battery is reduced, and the cycle life of the lithium ion battery is prolonged.

In the invention, the infiltration coefficient of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece can be measured by the following method: filling electrolyte into a dropper with a certain inner diameter and standard scales; fully drying the positive pole piece (for example, drying at 70-90 ℃ for 10-15 h), and then cutting a square positive pole piece with a sufficient area; in a drying room with the humidity lower than 2%, the lower opening of the dropper is in contact with the square positive pole piece, the dropper is ensured to be perpendicular to the surface of the square positive pole piece, the electrolyte in the dropper is gradually infiltrated into the square positive pole piece, the quality of the electrolyte infiltrated into the square positive pole piece every second is recorded, and the quality is the infiltration coefficient of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece.

The infiltration coefficient of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece can be realized by adjusting parameters such as porosity of the positive pole piece, BET (surface area emission) of the positive pole piece, viscosity of the electrolyte, surface tension of the electrolyte and the like and adjusting physical parameters of the electrolyte according to the microstructure of the positive pole piece. Those skilled in the art, based on the present disclosure, can reasonably determine how to adjust the parameters to obtain a suitable wetting coefficient. For example, generally, the higher the viscosity, the lower the wet coefficient, all other things being equal; and vice versa.

In some preferred embodiments, the viscosity of the electrolyte solution is 5mPa · s or less at 25 ± 3 ℃. More preferably, the viscosity of the electrolyte solution at 25. + -. 3 ℃ is not more than 4.5 mPas, 3 mPas or 3.5 mPas. Most preferably, the viscosity of the electrolyte is between 2.0 mPas and 5.0 mPas at 25 + -3 deg.C. The viscosity of the electrolyte can be determined by methods known in the art.

The inventors found that when the room temperature viscosity of the electrolyte is not more than 5mPa · s, the electrolyte is favorable for wetting the positive electrode sheet in a short time. Since the reduced decomposition product of the additive a is dissolved in the electrolyte and then infiltrates into the voids of the cathode active material along with the electrolyte, the wettability of the electrolyte, particularly the viscosity, affects the movement speed of the decomposition product. The better the electrolyte wettability (the lower the viscosity), the more favorable the decomposition products reach the exposed area of the current collector, and the current collector is protected.

The surface tension of the electrolyte can be achieved by selecting an appropriate organic solvent. In some embodiments, the organic solvent in the electrolyte may be used without limitation. Organic solvents commonly used in the art are generally used. Some examples of organic solvents that may be used include, but are not limited to: dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), dipropyl carbonate (DPC), Ethyl Methyl Carbonate (EMC), propyl methyl carbonate (MPC), propyl ethyl carbonate (EPC), ethylene carbonate (VEC), Ethylene Carbonate (EC), Propylene Carbonate (PC), gamma-butyrolactone (GBL), Butylene Carbonate (BC), fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), Methyl Formate (MF), ethyl formate, Methyl Acetate (MA), Ethyl Acetate (EA), Propyl Acetate (PA), Methyl Propionate (MP), Ethyl Propionate (EP), Propyl Propionate (PP), Methyl Butyrate (MB), Ethyl Butyrate (EB), Sulfolane (SF), dimethyl sulfone (MSM), methyl ethyl sulfone (EMS), diethyl sulfone (ESE), Tetrahydrofuran (THF) and propylene sulfite. From a practical and commercial point of view, it is preferred that the non-aqueous organic solvent is a carbonate, or a mixture of a carbonate and a carboxylic acid ester. In some preferred embodiments, the organic solvent is 65% to 85% by mass in the electrolyte.

The above electrolyte may be prepared according to a conventional method in the art. The electrolyte can be obtained by uniformly mixing an organic solvent, electrolyte lithium salt and optional additives. Wherein the order of addition of the materials is not particularly limited. For example, the electrolyte lithium salt and optional additives are added into an organic solvent and mixed uniformly to obtain the electrolyte. The electrolyte lithium salt may be added to the organic solvent first, and then the optional additives may be added to the organic solvent separately or simultaneously.

The inventors have found that, compared to the above high nickel cathode material and low operating voltage (cell charge cut-off voltage V ≦ 4.2V), the low nickel cathode material has a stable structure, a low amount of lithium removal during charging and discharging in a low voltage system, less surface side reactions during charging and discharging, a low energy density, and does not achieve the excellent effects described herein when combined with other preferred features herein, but rather increases the cost.

Generally, the positive electrode sheet includes a conductive agent and a binder in addition to the positive active material. If necessary, a solvent and other additives, such as N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP), PTC thermistor material, and the like, may also be incorporated into the positive electrode sheet active material.

The conductive agent is not particularly limited as long as it exhibits conductivity without causing chemical changes in the battery. Suitable examples of conductive agents include, but are not limited to, graphite, such as natural graphite or artificial graphite; graphene; carbon black-based materials such as carbon black, Super P, acetylene black, ketjen black, and the like; conductive fibers such as carbon fibers, metal fibers, or carbon nanotube conductive fibers; metal powders such as aluminum or nickel powders; conductive whiskers such as zinc oxide, potassium titanate, and the like; conductive metal oxides such as iron oxide; polyphenylene derivatives and the like; and any combination thereof. In the positive electrode sheet active material layer of the battery, the weight of the conductive agent may be 0% to 4%, preferably 1% to 3%, of the total weight of the positive electrode sheet active material layer.

The binder is not particularly limited as long as it plays a binding role and does not cause chemical changes in the battery. The binder is selected from one or more of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene copolymer (PVDF-co-HEP), polyvinylidene fluoride, polyacrylonitrile, polymethyl methacrylate, polyvinyl alcohol, carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), starch, hydroxypropyl fiber, regenerated cellulose, polyvinylpyrrolidone, polytetrafluoroethylene, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyacrylic acid, Styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR), fluorinated rubber, ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer, polyurethane, and copolymers thereof. In the positive electrode sheet active material layer of the battery, the weight of the binder may be 0% to 4%, preferably 1% to 3%, of the total weight of the positive electrode sheet active material layer.

In some preferred embodiments, the porosity of the positive electrode sheet is 13% to 40%, more preferably 15% to 37%. In some exemplary embodiments, the porosity of the positive electrode sheet may be, for example, 18%, 20%, 24%, 26%, 38%, 30%, or 34%.

In some preferred embodiments, the specific surface area of the positive electrode plate is 0.5m2/g～1.5m2(ii) in terms of/g. The larger the specific surface area of the positive pole piece is, the easier the electrolyte is to be absorbed, and the infiltration of the electrolyte on the positive pole piece can be accelerated. By setting the specific surface area of the positive pole piece to 0.5m2/g～1.5m2And the electrolyte can quickly infiltrate the positive pole piece, the contact area of the positive active material layer and the electrolyte can be controlled within a reasonable range, and the side reaction of the electrolyte and the positive pole piece is effectively prevented.

In the invention, the specific type, thickness and composition of the diaphragm are not particularly limited, and can be selected according to actual requirements. Specifically, the separator may be selected from a polyethylene film, a polypropylene film, a polyvinylidene fluoride film, and a multi-layer composite film thereof.

In the battery of the present invention, the negative active material may be selected from soft carbon, hard carbon, (artificial or natural) graphite, silicon oxy-compound, silicon carbon composite, lithium titanate, metal capable of forming an alloy with lithium, and the like. Specifically, a carbon-based material, a silicon-based material, a tin-based material, or the like can be used. Preferably, graphite is used as the negative active material. However, the present application is not limited to these materials, and other conventionally known materials that can be used as a negative electrode active material for a lithium ion battery may be used. These negative electrode active materials may be used alone or in combination of two or more.

2. Performance testing

(1) High-temperature gas production performance test of lithium ion battery

Under the condition of room temperature (25 ℃), the lithium ion battery is charged to 4.3V at a constant current of 1C, and then charged to a current of 0.05C at a constant voltage of 4.3V. After the cell was fully charged, the initial volume of the cell was tested using a drainage method. After the batteries were stored in an oven at 80 ℃ for 10 days, the batteries were taken out. The mixture was allowed to stand at room temperature for 60 minutes. The cell volume was tested by draining within 60 minutes after cooling to room temperature.

And (5) performing storage test according to the steps until 30 days of storage. And calculating the volume expansion rate of the battery along with the storage time by taking the volume of the battery tested before storage as a reference. The lithium ion battery stored at 80 ℃ for a certain number of days, and then the volume expansion ratio (%) (battery volume measured after storage on the N-th day/battery volume measured before storage) -1.

(2) Low-temperature power performance test of lithium ion battery

Under room temperature conditions, the lithium ion battery was charged at a constant current of 1C to 4.3V, and then charged at a constant voltage of 4.3V to a current of 0.05C. After the battery is fully charged, standing for 5min, discharging at 1C for 30min (the electric quantity of a battery core is 50% SOC), and then standing for 5 min. And regulating the temperature to-20 ℃, standing for 1h, and recording the voltage V1 of the battery cell at the moment. When the voltage V2 after pulse discharge is recorded at 0.4C for 15s, DCR (V1-V2)/I (I) when the battery cell is discharged at 50% SOC for 15s is 0.4C.

(3) Viscosity measurement

Firstly, 30mL of electrolyte is taken, the electrolyte is subjected to constant temperature for 30min under a constant-temperature water bath at 25 ℃, the electrolyte is added into a liquid adding cup of a viscometer and is simultaneously connected with a constant-temperature water bath kettle, so that the temperature of the liquid adding cup is constant, a rotor and the rotating speed of the viscometer are set, and after 10min, the reading on an instrument panel of the viscometer, namely the viscosity of the electrolyte at the temperature, is read.

(4) Coefficient of infiltration test

Filling electrolyte into a capillary tube with an inner diameter d and standard scales, and recording the height of the electrolyte in the capillary tube as h; fully drying the positive pole piece (for example, drying at 70-90 ℃ for 10-15 h), and then cutting a square positive pole piece of 5cm multiplied by 5 cm; in a drying room with the humidity lower than 2%, enabling a lower opening of a dropper to be in contact with a square positive pole piece, ensuring that the dropper is perpendicular to the surface of the square positive pole piece, gradually infiltrating electrolyte in the dropper into the square positive pole piece, recording the time t for the electrolyte to be completely absorbed, and calculating the infiltration coefficient pi of the electrolyte on the surface of the positive pole piece in the unit of mu g/s according to the following formula:

V＝π*(d/2)2*h*ρ/t

v: electrolysisLiquid absorption rate (μ g/s), d: capillary diameter (cm), h: electrolyte height (cm), ρ: density of electrolyte (g/cm)3) And t: electrolyte absorption time(s).

(5) Cycle performance test

At 25 ℃, the lithium ion battery was tested after being fully discharged at 1C. The test process is as follows: charging the lithium ion battery to a voltage of 4.3V at a constant current of 1C, then charging to a current of 0.05C at a constant voltage of 4.3V, standing for 5min, and discharging the lithium ion battery to a voltage of 3.0V at a constant current of 1C, wherein the process is a charge-discharge cycle process, and the discharge capacity of the time is the discharge capacity of the first cycle. And (4) carrying out a plurality of times of cyclic charge and discharge tests on the lithium ion battery according to the method until the discharge capacity of the lithium ion secondary battery is attenuated to 80%, and recording the cycle times of the lithium ion battery.

From the test results in Table 3, it can be seen that the overall performance of examples 1 to 22 is improved as compared with the high temperature storage gassing performance and the low temperature DCR obtained in the test of comparative examples 1 to 5. It was shown that the content of impurity element copper atom in aluminum foil of the positive electrode current collector using the specific fluorine-containing lithium sulfonimide salt defined in the present invention as the first lithium salt and the additive a and defining a unit area was 0.009g/m2～0.021g/m2When the amount is within the range of (1), the low-temperature power performance and the high-temperature storage performance of the battery can be effectively improved.

In comparative examples 1 and 2, the fluorine-containing organic lithium salt is not used as the main lithium salt, the conductivity of the electrolyte is low, and the stability of the electrolyte is poor, so that the storage gassing and power performance of the electrolyte are poor. Comparative example 3 contains no additive a, resulting in that the electrolyte containing the lithium salt of fluorosulfonylimide directly contacts the aluminum foil through the micropores between the cathode active particles, thereby corroding the aluminum foil, and on the other hand, film formation at the cathode interface, i.e., electrolyte decomposition, cannot be suppressed. Therefore, the storage gassing and power performance of comparative example 3 were poor. In comparative example 4, the content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil of the positive electrode current collector per unit area is too high, which accelerates corrosion of the aluminum foil, promotes oxidative decomposition of the electrolyte, and the decomposition product is deposited on the interface to cause higher impedance, which deteriorates power performance of the battery cell, and the electrolyte decomposes to generate gas, which deteriorates storage performance of the battery cell. In comparative example 5, the content of impurity element copper atoms in the aluminum foil of the positive current collector per unit area is too low, and the mechanical strength of the current collector is too low, so that the extensibility of the current collector is too high in the processing process of the pole piece, and the current collector bears too large stress and poor current conductivity in the cycle process of the battery, so that the DRC (design control rate) of the lithium ion battery is increased and the long-term cycle performance is obviously deteriorated.

From the results of examples 2 and 9 to 11, it can be further seen that the content of copper atoms as an impurity element per unit area in the aluminum foil of the positive electrode current collector was 0.016g/m under the same conditions2And 0.013g/m2Reduced to 0.009g/m2The high-temperature storage gas production performance is gradually kept stable, but the cycle performance is continuously reduced. Therefore, the content of impurity copper atoms per unit area of the aluminum foil is more preferably 0.013g/m2To 0.021g/m2In the range, for example, about 0.016g/m2Thereby obtaining excellent balance between the high-temperature storage gas production performance and the cycle performance of the battery.

In addition, the inventors have found that the use of a different lithium salt of a fluorine-containing sulfonimide (e.g., lithium methyltrifluoromethylsulfonimide or lithium bis-fluorosulfonimide) as the first lithium salt has less effect on the performance of the battery under otherwise identical conditions. In particular, as shown in examples 4 and 5, the performance of the battery was substantially the same under otherwise identical conditions using lithium methyltrifluoromethylsulfonyl imide or lithium bis-fluorosulfonimide as the first lithium salt.

The above results show that: the comprehensive performance of the battery cell can be effectively improved only by jointly using the fluorine-containing sulfimide lithium salt and the additive A and controlling the content of impurity element copper atoms in the positive current collector aluminum foil in unit area within a specific range.
